headline: Shenzhou-24 Launches With Pakistani Payload Specialist
deck: The crewed spacecraft left Jiuquan atop a Long March-2F for Tiangong, completing the scheduled launch reported Tuesday.
body: China launched Shenzhou-24 on Wednesday, sending three astronauts toward the Tiangong space station; the crew included Pakistani astronaut Muhammad Zeeshan Ali [E1][E3]. The spacecraft lifted off from the Jiuquan Satellite Launch Center atop a Long March-2F carrier rocket [E2].

The other crew members are mission commander and spacecraft pilot Tang Hongbo and flight engineer Wu Yi; news.cn described Ali as the first foreign astronaut to visit Tiangong [E3]. The mission is the first joint flight of Chinese and foreign astronauts in China’s manned space program [E4].

The paper’s 24 November coverage reported that Shenzhou-24 was scheduled to lift off on Wednesday from Jiuquan [E7]; Wednesday’s liftoff completes that planned flight. Pakistan’s space agency listed the mission for 05:18 PKT, with Tiangong as the destination and a payload-specialist role [E5], and said Ali had been selected as the first Pakistani astronaut for an orbital mission [E6].
